name: Burning Steppes
summary: The Burning Steppes are a scorched, volcanic wasteland flanking the southern base of Blackrock Mountain. Formed by the catastrophic summoning of Ragnaros centuries ago, this treacherous territory holds the primary overland passage between Stormwind and Khaz Modan. Today, it crawls with rogue Blackrock orcs, Firegut ogres, Dark Iron dwarves, and broodlings of the black dragonflight.

sections.title: A Cataclysmic Origin
sections.body: Long ago, these foothills were simply the northern reaches of the Redridge Mountains. During the War of the Three Hammers, the exiled Dark Iron clan established their kingdom here, raising their capital city of Thaurissan. Facing total defeat at the hands of the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans, the desperate Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan attempted to conjure elemental forces. Instead, he shattered the earth and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord into Azeroth. The violent explosion pulverized the surrounding mountains, tore open rivers of lava, and birthed the colossal volcano known as Blackrock Mountain, leaving the steppes forever charred and barren.

sections.title: Echoes of the Second War
sections.body: During the Second War, the Old Horde claimed Blackrock Spire as its foremost seat of power. At the climax of the conflict, the Grand Alliance of Lordaeron pushed deep into the Burning Steppes to lay siege to the mountain. It was at the foot of Blackrock Mountain that Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer clashed with Lord Anduin Lothar, striking down the human champion. Rather than breaking the Alliance's resolve, Lothar's death galvanized the Allied armies to rout the orcs, sealing the victory of the Second War and leaving behind an enduring valley of ash and rusted steel.

sections.title: A Den of Monsters and Dragons
sections.body: Though Thrall established a New Horde in distant Kalimdor, the Blackrock clan remaining in the steppes maintains the bloodthirsty cruelty of the Old Horde. Operating from Blackrock Stronghold, these orcs openly ally with the black dragonflight and local Firegut ogres rather than honor any truce. Meanwhile, Dark Iron dwarves and elemental servitors lurk among the fiery ruins, all while black drakes and wyrmkin prey upon unwary travelers attempting to use the thoroughfare to cross between Stormwind and the northern kingdoms.

faq.q: Why is the ground charred and covered in lava?
aliases: why is blackrock mountain a volcano
faq.answer: Centuries ago, the Dark Iron Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan attempted to summon an elemental minion to rescue his clan from defeat in the War of the Three Hammers. His spell mistakenly breached the Elemental Plane and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord, ripping open the earth, creating the massive Blackrock volcano, and reducing the northern Redridge Mountains to a charred wasteland.

faq.q: Do the orcs here belong to Thrall's Horde?
faq.answer: No. The orcs in the Burning Steppes are remnants of the Blackrock clan who refuse to join Thrall's New Horde. They do not honor the armistice with the Alliance and remain dedicated to the savage, warmongering traditions of the First and Second Wars, serving Blackrock Spire and the black dragonflight.

Anduin Lothar was slain by Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer at the foot of Blackrock Mountain in the Burning Steppes near the end of the Second War. Lothar's demise spurred his second-in-command, Turalyon, and the Alliance forces into a furious counterattack that shattered the Horde's lines.

faq.q: Where can the Alliance find shelter in the steppes?
faq.answer: Alliance soldiers and travelers base themselves at Morgan's Vigil, an elevated outpost in the southeastern foothills of the zone. Marshal Maxwell commands the station, watching over the northern pass and monitoring enemy troop movements around the mountain.

faq.q: Where does the Horde stage operations here?
faq.answer: Horde adventurers report to Flame Crest, an elevated camp located along the northeastern ridge. From here, emissaries watch the rival Blackrock clan and maintain flight connections back to the Badlands, the Swamp of Sorrows, and Searing Gorge.

faq.q: What are the Ruins of Thaurissan?
aliases: what is the destroyed dwarf city
faq.answer: The Ruins of Thaurissan are the remnants of the grand city built by the Dark Iron clan after their exile from Ironforge. When Thane Thaurissan summoned Ragnaros, the raw elemental blast destroyed his capital and enslaved his surviving people to the Firelord's will.

angles.text: The Burning Steppes are a somber, dangerous frontier where Supreme Commander Anduin Lothar fell; Marshal Maxwell at Morgan's Vigil continually seeks brave champions to counter the threats encroaching toward Redridge.
Thrall's New Horde watches Flame Crest with deep concern, determined to curb the dangerous, unrepentant Blackrock clan whose warmongering stains the honor of orckind.
Every stone in the steppes bears witness to the Dark Iron clan's folly during the War of the Three Hammers, culminating in the shattering of their capital and the summoning of Ragnaros.
The volcanic landscape is rich in rare minerals, making it one of the select open-air regions on Azeroth to harvest valuable Dark Iron deposits alongside veins of rich thorium.
